1.explanation: The bug manifests in syntax highlighting and comment parsing issues for Scala and JavaScript. The files likely to be involved based on the repo structure are: 1) 'src/languages/scala.js' and 'src/languages/javascript.js' as these define the language-specific parsing rules for comments and class declarations; 2) 'src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js' since JavaScript may extend or use generic ECMAScript parsing logic; 3) 'src/lib/html_renderer.js' as this handles rendering the parsed tokens and any errors in token type assignment will show up in the HTML output; and 4) 'src/lib/mode_compiler.js' since it processes the language definitions and builds the tokenization engine, which might have logic bugs causing comments to be misclassified in edge cases (such as inside parameter lists or on the same line as a declaration). These files together control the core token parsing, classification, and rendering steps responsible for the reported issues.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario is that language comments in certain cases are rendered incorrectly, as seen in both Scala and JavaScript highlighting contexts. For Scala, when a comment is on the same line as the class definition (but before the opening curly brace), each word of the comment is rendered as a class title instead of being shown as a comment. For JavaScript, comments inside function parameter lists are not being highlighted as comments; instead they're rendered as plain text, losing syntax highlighting. The attached image demonstrates such an issue where comments to the right of parameters are not highlighted appropriately in JavaScript.

2.explanation:
- src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js: Contains the core grammar and parsing logic for ECMAScript-based languages (like JavaScript); an error here could prevent proper tokenization of comments, especially in nuanced contexts like function params.
- src/languages/javascript.js: The syntax highlighting definition for JavaScript; any deficiencies or edge cases in comment handling would likely be here.
- src/languages/scala.js: The syntax highlighting definition for Scala; the problem with class titles and inline comments relates directly to its parsing logic.
- src/lib/html_renderer.js: Responsible for rendering parsed token trees into HTML; a misclassification here might render comments as a different type (e.g., title, identifier) in the output markup.
- src/lib/token_tree.js: Manages the structure of tokens returned from language parsing; issues here could result in comments not being assigned the correct type (i.e., 'comment'), affecting rendering regardless of the language definition.
2.bug_scenario: The primary issue described in the bug report is that comments are not properly highlighted in specific scenarios: (1) In Scala, comments after the class title (when curly brace is not on the same line) are incorrectly rendered as part of the class title. (2) In JavaScript, comments within parameter lists are not highlighted as comments at all—they appear as normal text, not in the comment style. The attached image further demonstrates that comments inside the parameter list of a JavaScript function are rendered in regular text color and not in comment-style coloring, confirming the bug with comment parsing in this context.
